name: Paint needed
description: Estimates the liters of paint required as wall area ÷ coverage per liter × number of coats. It accounts for painting the surface multiple times.
notes: Coverage varies with surface porosity and paint type; the estimate ignores waste and touch-ups, so round up when buying.

name: Wall area (four walls)
description: Computes the combined area of the four walls of a rectangular room as 2 × (length + width) × height, i.e. the perimeter times the wall height.
notes: Does not subtract doors or windows, so it overestimates the paintable surface. Assumes a rectangular room with uniform wall height.

name: Room floor area
description: Calculates the floor area of a rectangular room by multiplying its length by its width.
notes: Valid only for rectangular floors; irregular shapes must be split into rectangles and summed. Both dimensions must share the same unit.

name: Tiles needed
description: Estimates how many tiles are needed by dividing floor area by the area of one tile, adding a waste margin, and rounding up to a whole number of tiles.
notes: Enter the waste margin as a percentage; the ceiling function ensures a whole tile count. Cuts, breakage, and pattern matching may require an even larger margin.

name: Wallpaper rolls
description: Estimates the number of wallpaper rolls needed by dividing total wall area by the area one roll covers and rounding up to a whole roll.
notes: Ignores pattern repeat and trimming waste, which can increase the count. The ceiling function rounds up so partial rolls become full rolls.

name: Concrete volume
description: Calculates the volume of a rectangular concrete slab or pour as length × width × depth, giving the amount of concrete in cubic meters.
notes: All three dimensions must be in meters to yield cubic meters. Order extra to allow for spillage, uneven subgrade, and formwork variation.

name: Mulch/soil volume
description: Computes the volume of mulch or soil for a bed as area × depth / 100, converting a depth given in centimeters and an area in square meters into cubic meters.
notes: Depth must be entered in centimeters; the division by 100 converts it to meters. Loose materials settle, so buy slightly more than the calculated volume.

name: BTU for room cooling
description: Estimates the cooling capacity in BTU needed for a room by multiplying its floor area by a BTU-per-square-meter factor.
notes: The factor is a rough rule of thumb; sunlight, ceiling height, occupancy, and insulation all change the real requirement. Use it only for initial sizing.

name: Air changes per hour
description: Calculates how many times a room's air is fully replaced each hour as airflow × 60 / room volume, using airflow in cubic meters per minute.
notes: Airflow must be in m3/min (the ×60 converts to per hour) and volume in m3. Higher air changes per hour mean better ventilation.

name: Building Coverage Ratio
description: Computes the building coverage ratio, the percentage of a site's area covered by a building's footprint, as footprint area divided by site area times 100. It is a key zoning limit on ground-floor building extent.
notes: Both areas must share the same unit (square metres). Local zoning codes set a maximum allowable percentage that the building footprint may not exceed.

name: Floor Area Ratio
description: Computes the floor area ratio, the percentage relationship between a building's total floor area across all stories and its site area, as total floor area divided by site area times 100. It caps the overall building bulk permitted on a site.
notes: Total floor area sums the floor area of every story, including basements per local code definitions. Both areas must share the same unit (square metres); zoning codes set a maximum allowable percentage.

name: U-Value of a Layered Wall
description: Gives the thermal transmittance of a wall or roof from the thickness and conductivity of each layer plus surface resistances (ISO 6946).
notes: Insulation layers dominate the result.

name: Solar Heat Gain through Glazing
description: Gives the solar heat entering through a window — a major summer cooling load and a winter bonus.
notes: External shading cuts g far more than internal blinds.

name: Number of Stair Risers
description: Computes the least number of steps for a staircase so that no riser is higher than the allowed maximum.
notes: The maximum riser height is set by local building rules. All risers in a flight should be equal.

name: Stair Riser Height
description: Computes the height of each riser when the total rise is divided into equal steps.
notes: Equal risers matter for safety; a step that differs by even a few millimetres can cause trips.

name: Blondel's Stair Formula (Step Length)
description: Computes Blondel's step length, twice the riser plus the going, used to check that a stair is comfortable to climb.
notes: From François Blondel (1675). Values of about 600–650 mm, close to a natural stride, are usually considered comfortable.

name: Energy to Heat Water
description: Computes the energy needed to heat a volume of water by a temperature rise, taking 1 L of water as 1 kg with a specific heat of 4.186 kJ/(kg·K).
notes: Heat losses from the tank and pipes are not included, so the energy actually used is higher.

name: Water Heater Heating Time
description: Computes how long an electric water heater takes to heat a volume of water by a temperature rise.
notes: Efficiency is a fraction (0.95 = 95 %). A heat pump water heater uses its coefficient of performance (COP) in place of efficiency, which is above 1.

name: Gravel or Sand by Weight
description: Computes the weight of gravel, sand or soil needed to fill an area to a depth, from its bulk density.
notes: Bulk density depends on the material and its moisture; dry gravel and sand are often about 1.5–1.7 t/m³.

name: Bricks Needed for a Wall
description: Computes the number of bricks for a single-thickness wall from the brick face size plus the mortar joint.
notes: A UK brick (215 × 65 mm) with 10 mm joints gives about 59 bricks per m². Add an allowance for cuts and breakage.

name: Fence Posts Needed
description: Computes the number of posts for a straight fence so that no gap between posts exceeds the maximum spacing.
notes: The extra post closes the far end. Each corner or gate needs its own count.

name: Deck Boards Needed
description: Computes the number of deck boards laid side by side to cover the width of a deck.
notes: This counts full-length rows; if the deck is longer than one board, multiply by the boards per row.

name: Rainwater Harvest from a Roof
description: Computes the rainwater that can be collected from a roof: 1 mm of rain on 1 m² is 1 L.
notes: The runoff coefficient covers losses from evaporation, splash and first-flush diversion; about 0.8 is often used for pitched roofs.

name: Ladder Base Distance (1-in-4 Rule)
description: Computes how far the foot of a leaning ladder should be from the wall: one unit out for every four units up.
notes: The 1-in-4 rule puts the ladder at about 76° to the ground; UK HSE guidance gives the angle as 75°.

name: Board Feet of Lumber
description: Computes lumber volume in board feet; one board foot is 1 in × 12 in × 1 ft (144 cubic inches).
notes: Nominal sizes are normally used for pricing, even though the actual planed size is smaller.

name: Maximum Total Floor Area from a Floor Area Ratio
description: Computes the largest total floor area allowed on a site from the floor area ratio limit.
notes: The limit is set by local planning rules, and other rules such as road width or height limits can lower it further.

name: Insulation Thickness for a Target U-Value

variables.label: Thermal resistance of the other layers

description: Computes the insulation thickness needed for a wall or roof to reach a target U-value, given the resistance of its other layers.
notes: The other layers include the inside and outside surface resistances. Thermal bridges such as studs are ignored.

name: Swimming Pool Volume
description: Computes the water volume of a rectangular pool with a uniform slope from the shallow end to the deep end.
notes: Uses the average of the two depths; a pool with a steep drop or a hopper holds a different amount.

name: Bags of Premixed Concrete
description: Computes the number of bags of premixed concrete for a volume, from the yield printed on the bag.
notes: Yield depends on bag size and product; check the bag. Add a little extra for uneven ground.

name: Roof Pitch Angle
description: Converts a roof pitch given as rise over run into an angle in degrees.
notes: In Japan a pitch is often written as rise per 10 of run (for example 4 sun); in North America as rise per 12 in.

name: Wood Moisture Content (Oven-Dry Basis)
description: Computes the moisture content of wood as the weight of water divided by the oven-dry weight, the standard basis for timber.
notes: The oven-dry method (for example ASTM D4442) dries the sample at 103 ± 2 °C to constant weight. Firewood is usually burned below about 20 %.
